title: Tariff Rule: Application and Practitioner Certification for Medical and Life-Support Protections
content:
## 1. Where a protection may be registered

1.1 A protection under Medical and Life-Support Protections may be registered only on a residential service agreement in active, notice pending or disconnected status whose rate schedule is among the schedules on which the protection may be registered, for a patient who meets the protection's household requirement (who the patient must be in relation to the service address).

1.2 Applications are accepted only for a service agreement that is not closed or pending start. The status is read from the company's record of the service agreement named in the application, before the application is accepted.

| Status of the service agreement | Application |
|---|---|
| active | accepted |
| notice pending | accepted |
| disconnected | accepted |
| closed | not accepted |
| pending start | not accepted |

An application records the customer of record on the service agreement, the service agreement where the patient lives, the protection applied for by its full name, the application date and the number of qualifying devices stated on the application; the certification then stands in pending certification status.

## 2. Who certifies

2.1 The protection becomes active only on a certification from a practitioner among those whose certification the protection accepts, whose license number passes the protection's license check. The customer's own statement never substitutes for it.

2.2 Registration records the date the practitioner signed (or verbally gave) the certification as the certified date, the expiration date, the certifying practitioner's license number as written on the form, and the date the certification was registered.

## 3. Time allowed for the certification

3.1 A valid certification must be received no later than the certification due period after the application date. The period is counted in calendar days from the day after the application date, and a certification received on the last day is in time. The application date is taken from the company's record of the application.

3.2 An application for which no valid certification arrived within the certification due period is denied, with the reason recorded.

3.3 Where verbal certification is accepted for the protection, a practitioner's call registers the protection, which lapses as denied if the written form does not follow within the written follow-up period.

**Boundary cases (hypothetical dates).**

| Certification due period | Application date | Day 1 of the period | Last day of the period | Certification received | In time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 7 days | 10 June | 11 June | 17 June | 17 June | yes |
| 7 days | 10 June | 11 June | 17 June | 18 June | no |
| 30 days | 1 March | 2 March | 31 March | 31 March | yes |
| 30 days | 1 March | 2 March | 31 March | 1 April | no |

## 4. Expiration date

4.1 The expiration date is the certified date plus the protection's certification term in calendar months, less one day.

*Hypothetical:* a certification with a 12-month term certified on 15 March has the expiration date 14 March of the following year; with a 24-month term, 14 March two years later; with a 1-month term, 14 April.

## 5. Status outcomes

| Event | Status before | Status after |
|---|---|---|
| a valid practitioner certification is received and registered | pending certification | active |
| no valid certification arrived within the certification due period | pending certification | denied |
